chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq, from Harun ibn Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It suffices you from the ritual bath (Ghusl) and the cleansing (Istinja') what fills your right hand.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of water required for Ghusl and Istinja' according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides a practical, anthropometric standard for the minimum water volume required for Ghusl and Istinja', reflecting the Shia juristic principle of 'qalil al-ma'' (small quantity of water). By anchoring the ruling in the capacity of the right hand, it offers a tangible metric for daily ritual purity that balances sufficiency with the avoidance of israf (wastefulness), a key theme in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Yazeed Bin Is’haq, from Haroun Bin Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It would suffice you from the washing and the cleansing (after toilet) what fills your right hand’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Harun ibn Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
An amount of water which can fill up your right hand is sufficient for your Ghusl (bath) and washing clean your urethra.’”
